doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Indiana University with William Adam, then Hawaii and transcribing horn parts
summary: At Indiana he opened up beyond classical playing, then moved to Hawaii, formed a top 40 band and transcribed horn parts from records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: When — so I went to Indiana University and studied with this William Adam trumpet teacher, just the greatest man I’ve ever met. And nothing to do with trumpet, just a brilliant man in all aspects of life. And he kind of made you play trumpet for any occasion. You know you have to learn how to play trumpet before you can play the piccolo solo on “Penny Lane” or before you can play a jazz solo, or before you can play lead you’ve got to be able to play the trumpet. You know it’s about learning how to play the trumpet with him. So you were kind of set up as, I mean I went in as a classical trumpet player then heard these other guys playing, they would play in the orchestra, then they’d play first in the jazz bands at Indiana and they played jazz solos. And I go wow, those guys sound great and they’re playing all styles. That’s kind of what I want to do you know. So it was kind of an open door there for me to sort of spread my horizon from the legit world into whatever needs trumpet you know I’m kind of available for. So from then we moved — well I moved to Hawaii with one of the trumpet players that I met at Indiana and we started working over there and we formed a band over there and we’re playing some top 40 tunes, Aretha Franklin and Tower of Power and those kind of things. And we’ve got to have horn parts so I transcribed the horn parts from the record. And that was kind of the beginning of, you know, my really listening to records and kind of trying to understand how the horns sounded on those records and how can we do that.
